A cop and a kid have a little chat on the street during a parade. Washington, D.C. 1957 (XP from HistoricImages)

This photograph was taken during the Chinatown parade in D.C. when a 2 year old boy stepped out onto the street to get a better look at the dancing dragons. The officer bent over to warn him not to get to close and the boy, whose father was a Marine stationed in Japan, asked him if he was a Marine.

The rookie policeman went on to become the Chief of Police of Washington DC, Maurice Cullinane. The boy later was Orson Welles' Personal Assistant.

Called "Faith and Confidence" this image was snapped by photographer Bill Beall, who went to to win a Pulitzer Prize for it in 1958.
